text:
marta: Heads up — seeing a sharp rise in 429s on /v1/embeddings this morning correlated with rerank traffic. Dashboards: https://dash.re/redwood/embeds-latency. 95th went from ~120ms -> ~600ms, queue depth on gpu-pool-3 spiked to 240.

ops-bot: Alert: embeddings-service:429-rate > 5% (1m avg) — triggered at 08:13 UTC

samir: Is rerank using the same pool as embeddings? I thought we had lane isolation setup for heavy jobs.

jules: It is currently shared. Rerank jobs use batch_size=64 and full-attention; each job holds the GPU for ~1.4s on A100. Embeddings are tiny (~0.06s) but the long-running rerank batches are starving the queue.

kevin: We should split capacity — reserve a small hard pool for rerank and another for embeddings. Autoscaler today is soft, doesn't support strict partitioning.

anya: Could we do soft admission control first? e.g. token-buckets per-route that prioritize embeddings during spikes. Lower-priority rerank gets 429s or gets routed to a cheaper model.

samir: Agreed. Per-route token bucket + queue-length backpressure sounds good. If queue_length > 50 for embeddings -> deny low-priority rerank. Also consider max_wait thresholds to avoid head-of-line blocking.

marta: Also noticed cross-region fallback: traffic spilled to eu-central when us-west was saturated which increased RTT and caused extra timeouts. We should avoid cross-region spill for latency-sensitive routes.

jules: Proposed immediate changes: 1) Create a dedicated nodepool labeled rerank=true and pin rerank pods there. 2) Admission policy: embeddings get higher priority and a max_wait_ms of 200ms.

jules: Example rate-limiter prototype config (WIP):
```yaml
# per-route admission control prototype
- route: /v1/embeddings
  priority: high
  max_queue: 200
  token_rate: 500rps
  max_wait_ms: 200

- route: /v1/rerank
  priority: low
  max_queue: 50
  token_rate: 80rps
  max_concurrency: 8
```

ops-bot: Ticket created: PF-4876 — Allocate rerank nodepool, update autoscaler rules, and add per-route limiter.

kevin: Cost note — reserving 4 GPUs for a rerank pool will raise committed spend by ~ $9k/mo but should cut expensive over-provisioning during peaks and reduce customer 429s. Trade-off is predictable vs variable cost.

marta: Short-term mitigation: enable soft-throttle for rerank and fallback to quantized rerank model (q4f16) when embeddings SLO is breached. That reduces per-request GPU time.

anya: I'll open a canary PR for the admission-control middleware with metrics: per-route queue_depth, p99_wait, reroutes and a feature flag.

samir: Plan / Action items: @jules create the k8s nodepool and label it; @anya PR admission-control + dashboards; infra to update autoscaler policy to allow fixed minima for nodepools. We'll monitor for 1h post-deploy and roll back if errors increase.

jules: 👍 starting nodepool request now.

marta: Thanks all. Let's reconvene after the canary results. :+1:
